name: Castle of the Teutonic Order in Malbork
description: Malbork Castle, in northern Poland, is a vast red-brick fortress begun by the Teutonic Order in the 13th century and expanded after 1309, when the Grand Master moved in. It is the largest castle in the world by land area. Badly damaged in the Second World War, it was rebuilt using earlier conservators' detailed records, and its towers and walls now rise above the river Nogat.
